Before patching, our own wrapper ran and the output ends with: 'pre-patch-check: application ledgerd is in a change freeze until 2026-12-01, refusing to patch (exit 3)'. What should I run to fix it?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "c8511a63-eb2e-4ac1-9547-165393fbfb21", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Nothing needs fixing. Your wrapper did what it was built to do: it saw the `ledgerd` change freeze (until 2026-12-01) and refused to patch with exit 3. SSM then reported that non-zero exit as a failed `AWS-RunPatchBaseline` run. I wouldn't try to work around the check.

Here are your options, depending on what you need:

- **Wait for the freeze to end (most likely).** The freeze ends in 6 days. After 2026-12-01, rerun the patch or let your next maintenance window pick the instance up. If a Maintenance Window or State Manager association fires before then, expect it to fail the same way. You can move its schedule past the freeze, or temporarily remove the instance from that patch group.
- **Check compliance now without installing anything.** Run `AWS-RunPatchBaseline` with `Operation=Scan`. This reports which patches are missing and doesn't touch the freeze-protected app. Check that your wrapper doesn't also block scans, since some pre-patch hooks do.
- **Patch urgently, for example for a critical CVE.** Get a freeze exception approved by the `ledgerd` owner or your change board first. Then use whatever sanctioned override your wrapper has. I can't see the wrapper, so I won't guess at flags or tell you to edit or bypass it.

If you'd like, I can look at the full command invocation output for `i-1234567890abcdef0_4` to confirm the freeze check was the only failure. I can also look for other patch associations or maintenance windows that will hit the same block before Dec 1.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
